• export interface TimelineRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; offset: number; limit: number (1..100, the window cap); zoom: number (safe integer 1..8, cells per second); pan: number (safe integer >= 0, cells); columns: number (safe integer 8..200, bar cells); maxLanes?: number (1..64, default 16); maxRowsPerLane?: number (1..100, default 40); relationLimit?: number (1..100, default 40) }. Invalid values throw CapabilityError('validation') before any reader call.
• export function buildTimelineLanes(reader: TimelineReader, request: TimelineRequest): TimelineModel — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now, Math.random, process or environment reads; every timestamp comes from reader rows), calls reader.window exactly once and reader.relations at most once per returned node with {scope, to: node.key, limit: relationLimit}; never calls ingest/refresh/relate/markStale or any provider; returns a deeply frozen plain object that survives JSON round-trip losslessly.
• TimelineModel { contract; revision; topologyRevision; origin: { startedAt: string; basis: 'earliest-observed-start' } | { startedAt: null; basis: 'none' }; span: { ms: number | null; complete: boolean }; lanes: readonly TimelineLane[]; concurrency: { maxMeasured: number; basis: 'source-intervals-only'; countsOpenIntervals: true }; notes: readonly TimelineNote[]; truncated: { lanes: boolean; rows: boolean; relations: boolean; window: boolean } }.
• TimelineLane { key: string; label: string; basis: 'ownership' | 'grouping' | 'provider'; confirmed: boolean; rows: readonly TimelineRow[] }. Lane assignment per row: an incoming 'ownership' edge from a node in the same scope -> lane key = that parent's key, basis 'ownership'; else an incoming 'grouping' edge -> that parent's key, basis 'grouping'; else lane key `provider:${nativeRef.provider}`, basis 'provider'. When several parents of the chosen kind qualify, the lexicographically smallest parent key wins and note 'multiple-parents' is added; 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never assign a lane or alter timing. confirmed is true only when every edge used for the lane carries provenance.nativeConfirmationRef. Lane label is the parent's presentation.title (redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 80) when the parent is inside the window, else the sanitized parent key, else the provider name.
• TimelineRow { key; nativeRef; title (sanitized, max 80); tone: Presentation['statusTone']; freshness; timing: { kind: 'closed'; startedAt; endedAt; durationMs } | { kind: 'open'; startedAt } | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: 'no-source-interval' }; bar: { offsetCells; lengthCells; clippedLeft; clippedRight; openEnded } | null }. No field named elapsedMs, estimatedEndedAt or progressPercent exists anywhere in the model.
• Ordering: lanes by earliest row startedAt then key; rows inside a lane by startedAt then key; rows without an interval last, by key. Rows beyond maxRowsPerLane and lanes beyond maxLanes are dropped with truncated.rows / truncated.lanes true; truncated.window is total > offset + returned; truncated.relations is true when any relations page returned exactly relationLimit rows.
• Bar math: origin = earliest startedAt over rows with a parsable interval; offsetCells = floor((startedAt - origin)/1000 * zoom) - pan; closed lengthCells = max(1, floor(durationMs/1000 * zoom)); open bars extend to the right edge with openEnded true; bars are clipped to [0, columns) with clippedLeft/clippedRight flags; a bar entirely outside the viewport becomes bar null and note 'rows-outside-viewport' is added. Unparsable timestamps produce timing 'unavailable' (never a throw: the projection already validated dates).
• Concurrency: sweep over interval boundaries of the returned rows: a closed interval counts on [startedAt, endedAt), an open interval counts from startedAt to the latest known boundary; maxMeasured is the maximum simultaneous count; rows without intervals never count.
• Notes (frozen vocabulary, each at most once): 'clocks-may-differ' (present whenever intervals come from more than one nativeRef.provider), 'open-intervals-present', 'intervals-missing' (carries a count), 'stale-rows-present', 'window-partial', 'relation-page-full', 'multiple-parents', 'rows-outside-viewport', 'phase-kinds-unavailable' (always present: Interval carries no waiting/executing/blocked kinds, so lanes show source intervals only).

title: VC-1/W02-B: offline cancellation fault-injection conformance tier for the Claude SDK host and runtime abort path (cancel before session id, during tool use, after streamed text, late abort after result; per-agent isolation; requested/acknowledged/terminal ordering) over the fixture query seam with mutation proof; src untouched
description:

The code paths exist and are all uncovered: claude-host.ts:133 (config.signal already aborted -> skipped, zero queries), :156-158 (one AbortController per agent, linked once to config.signal), :171 (abortController handed to the SDK), :190 (stream loop), :207-208 (stream ends without a result while aborted -> "Claude SDK query was cancelled."), :218 (terminal result arrived but the controller was aborted -> cancelled, never ok), :247-250 (thrown error while aborted -> cancelled, otherwise failed), :252-253 (listener removed, controller dropped), :268-269 (abortAgent aborts only its own controller, unknown id is a no-op); src/workflow/runtime.ts:323 (RunWorkflowOptions.signal), :852-853 (finish aborts every in-flight agent), :865-867 (onAbort -> status "killed", "Workflow aborted."), :1113/:1165 (inflight add/delete). test/workflow-borrowed.test.ts:565 pins status killed only.

Scope (atomic, test-only, hot-file free, src/ untouched): ONE new vitest file test/workbench-claude-cancel-faults.test.ts plus ONE optional helper test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts (a controllable fake SDK stream: yields SDKMessage fixtures on demand, records whether options.abortController.signal fired, can honour the abort by rejecting or ignore it and finish). Every case drives the REAL createClaudeWorkflowHost with query injected through ClaudeWorkflowHostOptions.query, and the REAL runWorkflow where the runtime is the subject (a spy WorkflowHost only there). Never vi.mock of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, never Pi AgentManager, no network, no credentials.

Fault locations and expected outcomes (each its own named case):
F1 cancel BEFORE the init message (no session id yet): result {ok:false, skipped:true, error:"Claude SDK query was cancelled."} with no sessionId property; the fake stream saw abortController.signal.aborted === true.
F2 cancel DURING tool execution (after an assistant message carrying a tool_use block, before the user tool_result): cancelled result carries the sessionId the init message reported.
F3 cancel AFTER streamed assistant text, before the result message, SDK ends the stream on abort: cancelled — not "Claude SDK stream ended without a result message.", which the same stream yields without an abort (host-contract :152 pins that).
F4 LATE abort: the SDK yields its result message and finishes but the controller was aborted before return: result.skipped === true, result.ok is never true, sessionId retained; the host's session map does not record the agent, so a later agent({resume}) on it refuses through the existing unknown-session path.
F5 pre-aborted config.signal: zero query() calls, skipped result (claude-host.ts:133).
F6 per-agent isolation: two concurrent spawns; host.abortAgent('wf-agent-0') aborts only agent 0's controller (the two abortController objects handed to query() are distinct); agent 1 completes ok:true with its own sessionId; a repeated abortAgent on the same id and one on an unknown id are no-ops (no throw).
F7 config.signal aborts all owned agents: both per-agent controllers fire exactly once; each result is cancelled; an abort after both agents have settled fires no per-agent controller (listeners removed at :252).
F8 runtime path: runWorkflow(script with parallel([agent(), agent()]), host spy) whose signal is aborted once both spawns are in flight: outcome {status:"killed", error:"Workflow aborted."}, host.abortAgent called exactly once per in-flight agent and zero times for an agent that settled before the signal, no spawnAgent after the abort, onProgress never reports a cancelled agent as done; a second runWorkflow sharing the same host but a different signal is unaffected (its spawns complete ok:true).
F9 three phases, explicitly ordered: with onMessage/onSettled hooks and a monotonic counter (or vi.useFakeTimers), requestedAt (abort call) < acknowledgedAt (onSettled delivering skipped:true) < terminalAt (runWorkflow resolved) per cancelled agent; a fixture whose onSettled never fires is reported by the test as unacknowledged (proving the detection, never assuming the phase).

Red for a test-only bead is a MUTATION proof, recorded in the delivered ledger line as mutant -> red case names, with the source restored to HEAD bytes afterwards (git diff --stat vs 1fc74f0 lists only the new test files): M1 remove the `controller.signal.aborted` check at claude-host.ts:218 (late abort returns ok:true) -> F4 red; M2 drop `config.signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, ...)` at :158 -> F7 red; M3 share one AbortController across agents -> F6 red; M4 remove `for (const agentId of inflight) host.abortAgent(agentId)` at runtime.ts:853 -> F8 red; M5 remove the pre-aborted return at :133 -> F5 red.

If a case measures a GENUINE violation at HEAD (for example a late abort returning ok:true), do NOT edit src/: record the finding in the delivered ledger line and the bead notes and return blocked — the fix belongs to W02 (wb-7qs).

title: W13/VC-5: Claude session reader adapter projects agent-call, session and tool-use NativeSnapshots with observed ownership, causation and grouping edges from ClaudeNativeObservation (bounded, redacted, no invented ids); Pi observer wiring excluded
description:
Gap: `grep -rln NativeSnapshot src` at rig ad3cf6e returns only src/workbench/observation.ts and src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts. Claude is the one provider that has produced real native sessions (VC-1 measured) yet it has no reader adapter. src/index.ts:2676 (hot) consumes createClaudeObserver and ingests ONE flat 'claude.stream' event per sampled ClaudeNativeObservation whose source key flips from {pi-workflow, agent-call, `${task.id}:${index}`} before init to {claude-agent-sdk, session, sessionId} after init, with no relation between the two keys and no tool-use nodes at all; ClaudeNativeObservation.tools (toolUseId/name/state) never reaches the projection. The inspector therefore shows Claude work as disconnected flat rows: no agent-call -> session link and no session -> tool-use children, so wb-6ze.1's nested tree and wb-6ze.2's aggregates have nothing to nest for the provider that actually runs. docs/workbench/09 § Reader adapters lists Claude first ("SDK message events from sessions controlled by Workbench") and § Derived view indexes requires "allow local temporary ID before native assignment; rekey safely and preserve selection".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-topology.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-topology.test.ts; register and wire nothing.

- export type ClaudeObservedRelation = Parameters<ObservationProjection['relate']>[0];
- export interface ClaudeTopologyInput { call: ClaudeCallIdentity; snapshot: ClaudeNativeObservation; scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; observedAt: string; sequence: number; definitionDigest?: string; subjectBasis?: string }
- export interface ClaudeProjectionTopology { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ClaudeObservedRelation[]; truncated: boolean }
- export function projectClaudeTopology(input: ClaudeTopologyInput): ClaudeProjectionTopology — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now or Math.random; observedAt and sequence come from the caller), frozen result.
  • Agent-call snapshot ALWAYS: source {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call', id:`${invocationId}:${call.index}`} (the same key shape src/index.ts:2680 uses before init so existing rows keep their key); node {title: call.label through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 120 chars; type:'agent'; statusText: snapshot.terminal ?? 'observed-running'; statusTone: succeeded->success, failed->failure, cancelled/observation_lost->unknown, live->active}; kind 'claude.call'; trace {invocationId}; sequence; capturedAt and observedAt = input.observedAt; coverage 'partial' (the observer samples at most 64 snapshots per call); definitionDigest and subjectBasis passed through when supplied.
  • Session snapshot ONLY when snapshot.sessionId is a non-empty string: source {provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'session', id: sessionId}; node type 'agent', title `${label} · session`, same status mapping; kind 'claude.session'; evidenceRefs [`claude-message:${lastMessageId}`] only when lastMessageId exists; coverage 'unknown' when snapshot.freshness === 'unknown' else 'partial'. Never synthesize a session id from the agent id, pid, label or index.
  • One tool-use snapshot per snapshot.tools entry (<= 16 by construction), only when a session snapshot exists (a tool_use block is observed inside the session's native messages): source {provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'tool-use', id: toolUseId}; node {title: sanitized name, max 80; type:'sdk-operation'; statusText: the literal state ('started'|'completed'|'refused'|'failed'); statusTone: started->active, completed->success, failed->failure, refused->failure}; kind 'claude.tool-use'; trace {invocationId}.
  • Relations: ownership agent-call -> session with provenance {source:'pi-workflow', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: sessionId} (the workflow host that launched query() owns exactly that session; the SDK-reported session_id is the confirmation, satisfying the relate() rule at observation.ts:385 that provenance.source === from.provider and nativeConfirmationRef is present). Per tool-use: causation session -> tool-use with provenance {source:'claude-observer', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: toolUseId} AND grouping session -> tool-use with provenance {source:'claude-observer', observedAt} (display nesting; wb-6ze.1 nests on grouping/ownership only). No dependency or hypothesis edge is ever emitted; no edge references a node absent from `snapshots`.
  • truncated = snapshot.toolsTruncated; evicted tools are never invented.

Out of scope: editing src/index.ts (hot; the observer callback at :2676 is the parent's wiring point), src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/claude-transcript.ts, src/workflow/progress.ts, src/workbench/redaction.ts (import only), src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 edits it additively; this bead adds no projection API); transcript bodies, token counts, Pi tool output. title: W16-B/VC-4: pure bounded workflow_observe reply builder over ObservationProjection (cursor pagination, selectors, relation and event-window metadata, last-known-running + stale freshness summary, byte cap, sanitized compact JSON); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0): the registered workflow_observe tool (src/index.ts:2593-2622, hot) returns projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) nodes plus truncated and task fields, and furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2549-2570, hot) returns the raw FurnaceReading; neither offers a cursor, selectors, relation or event-window metadata, a freshness summary or a response byte cap, while W16 (wb-69g) names "compact bounded result and ACL" as its acceptance. docs/workbench/11 proposes workflow_observe(ref, selectors?, cursor?, limit?) returning "bounded native snapshot, event window, aggregates, freshness, anomaly evidence"; docs/workbench/09 requires Pi tool summaries to communicate "last-known-running + stale"; docs/workbench/14 lists "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries" as a benchmark measure. ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope, invocationId, offset, limit}) -> {nodes, total, revision} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope, from?, to?, limit?}) (:397), events({scope, limit, ref?, after?}) -> {events, truncated, completeness} (:540), relationRevision() (:467) and stats() (:558). The ACL (grants, session/workspace/principal checks) stays in the hot tool; this bead delivers the reply shaping the tool will later call.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observe-query.ts (new) exporting
- OBSERVE_CONTRACT = "workbench.observe/v1"; type ObserveReader = Pick<ObservationProjection, "window" | "relations" | "events" | "relationRevision" | "stats">.
- interface ObserveRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number (1..40, default 20); selectors?: { tone?: Presentation["statusTone"]; kind?: string; relations?: boolean; events?: { limit: number (1..40) } }; maxBytes?: number (1024..65536, default 16384) }.
- observeInvocation(reader: ObserveReader, request: ObserveRequest): ObserveReply, pure and synchronous: calls only reader methods (window once per call; relations at most once per returned node with limit <= 40 when selectors.relations; events once when selectors.events); never ingest/refresh/relate/markStale, never a provider.
- ObserveReply (frozen plain data, JSON round-trip lossless): { contract; invocationId; window: { offset; limit; returned; total; revision; nextCursor: string | null; truncated: boolean }; nodes: ObserveNode[] where ObserveNode = { key; nativeRef; kind; presentation (title and statusText passed through sanitizeWorkbenchText(value, 200) from src/workbench/redaction.ts; statusTone kept BESIDE statusText, never replacing it); freshness; completeness; sourceConnectionState; observedAt; lastConfirmedAt?; subjectBasis?; interval?; evidenceRefs (each sanitized, at most 20) ; evidenceTruncated: boolean }, never payloadRef bodies or event payloads; relations?: { perNode: { key; outgoing: Record<RelationKind, number>; partial: boolean }[]; basis: "returned-window-only" }; events?: { returned; truncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap"; kinds: Record<string, number>; providers: string[] } (metadata only: no event bodies, no node presentation copies); freshness: { current; stale; unknown; lastKnownRunningStale: number; summary: string } where lastKnownRunningStale counts returned nodes with statusTone "active" and freshness !== "current" and summary contains the literal "last-known-running + stale" whenever that count is > 0, otherwise "all returned nodes current" or "N stale / M unknown"; anomalies: { disconnectedProviders: string[]; partialCompleteness: number; eventGap: boolean; noRelationsAvailable: boolean }; aggregates: "not-wired" (literal until the ancestor-aggregate read model of wb-6ze.2 is wired by a later bead; no estimated numbers); countsBasis: "returned-window"; bytes: number; truncatedForBytes: boolean }.
- Cursor: opaque base64url of JSON { v: 1; offset; invocationId }, validated on decode; a malformed, negative, non-integer, cross-invocation or oversize (> 256 bytes) cursor throws CapabilityError("validation") from src/workbench/capability-registry.ts, never a silent restart at offset 0; nextCursor is null when offset + returned >= total.
- Byte cap: the reply is measured as Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(reply)); when over maxBytes, trim in this deterministic order - events, then relations, then nodes from the tail (adjusting window.returned/truncated and nextCursor so the dropped nodes are reachable on the next page) - and set truncatedForBytes true; never drop freshness, anomalies or window fields.
- No ANSI/control characters anywhere: JSON.stringify(reply) never matches /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f‮​]/ after sanitization.

Out of scope: registering or wiring the builder into workflow_observe/furnace_observe (src/index.ts, hot); ObservationProjection changes (src/workbench/observation.ts is being edited additively by wb-6ze.2 this round; import only); aggregates (wb-6ze.2) and their wiring; control actions (wb-69g.1); inspector rendering (wb-6ze.1/wb-g1g.1); any cap change.

Files: src/workbench/observe-query.ts (new); test/workbench-observe-query.test.ts (new). Fixtures: build a real ObservationProjection with refresh/ingest/relate/disconnect as test/workbench-observation.test.ts does.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observe-query.test.ts fails before src/workbench/observe-query.ts exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

O1. Bounded pagination over the projection, never the event history. A projection holding 95 nodes under one invocationId plus 100,000 ingested updates: observeInvocation with limit 20 returns 20 nodes, window.total 95 and a nextCursor; following nextCursor yields 95 distinct keys in viewport order and then nextCursor null; a reader spy shows exactly one window() call per reply with limit <= 40 and zero events()/relations() calls when selectors are absent; a cursor from another invocationId, a malformed string, a negative offset and a 300-byte cursor each throw CapabilityError with category "validation". Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Pi observation tools paginate/filter/limit and return compact JSON, never rendered ANSI." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-018: "Pi can query bounded semantic observations without consuming raw event logs or terminal-rendered text."

O2. Freshness nuance is spoken, not hidden. After disconnect("furnace") on a fixture with three active furnace nodes and two success forge nodes, freshness.lastKnownRunningStale === 3 and freshness.stale === 3; every returned furnace node keeps a statusText containing its native "RUNNING" text with statusTone "active" and freshness "stale"; freshness.summary contains the literal "last-known-running + stale"; after reconnect("furnace") alone the summary is unchanged; after a refresh() snapshot for one node the count drops to 2. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale. Pi tool summaries must communicate that nuance." Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Observation projection": "Do not replace native status with presentation.statusTone. This is a read model only."

O3. Relations and events are metadata, with partiality labelled. With selectors.relations true, a node carrying 3 grouping, 1 ownership (with nativeConfirmationRef) and 1 hypothesis outgoing edge reports perNode outgoing { grouping: 3, ownership: 1, hypothesis: 1, dependency: 0, causation: 0 } with partial false and basis "returned-window-only"; a node with 150 outgoing edges reports partial true (relations() page limit 40, never raised); with selectors.events { limit: 10 } over 1,000 ingested events, events.returned === 10, events.truncated true, events.kinds counts by kind, events.completeness "complete", and JSON.stringify(reply.events) contains no "presentation", "payload" or title text; an after-cursor whose event was evicted yields completeness "partial-gap" and anomalies.eventGap true. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Experimental projection implementation": "Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap." Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Missing edges do not imply independence." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-032: "Pi can use observer tools to inspect definition, retrieve bounded event windows, source/evidence refs and compare two runs."

O4. Response size is capped deterministically and honestly. With maxBytes 4096, selectors.relations and selectors.events set, and 40 nodes carrying 190-character titles: Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(reply)) <= 4096, truncatedForBytes true, events dropped before relations before nodes, window.returned === nodes.length, nextCursor points at the first dropped node so a following call returns it, and freshness/anomalies/window are always present; with maxBytes 65536 the same request fits and truncatedForBytes is false; maxBytes 512 or 1,000,000 throws CapabilityError "validation". Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Bound recursively nested JSON, bytes, array length, call count, response size and event rate." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Performance benchmark": "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries".

O5. Nothing leaks, nothing is executable. Titles and statusText containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E, U+200B and "Authorization: Bearer abc123" come back sanitized (no control, bidi or zero-width characters; "[REDACTED]" present and "abc123" absent) at most 200 characters; evidenceRefs are capped at 20 per node with evidenceTruncated true; JSON.stringify(reply) never matches /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f‮​]/ and contains no payloadRef body; the module source (read by the test) imports nothing from node:fs, node:child_process, node:net or any provider module. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default." Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Treat observed tool outputs as data, not instructions for Pi designer." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry": "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default."

O6. Scope isolation and read-only purity. A request whose scope differs from the nodes' scope returns window.total 0 and zero nodes without any relations()/events() call; a projection spy proves observeInvocation calls only window/relations/events/relationRevision/stats (never ingest, refresh, relate, markStale, disconnect, reconnect); two calls with identical inputs on an unchanged projection are deep-equal, and Object.isFrozen holds for the reply and its arrays. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-030: "Layout, reducers, status classification and control capabilities are pure/testable without a real terminal." Quote docs/workbench/03-architecture-and-ownership.md § "Design constraints": "An observation is a read, not a claim to cancel/control; explicit auth scope required for mutations."

O7. Measured counts only. countsBasis === "returned-window"; aggregates === "not-wired"; JSON.stringify(reply) contains no field named estimate, estimated, criticalPath, tokens or cost; window.total comes from window().total and window.revision from window().revision. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_observe(ref,selectors?,cursor?,limit?): bounded native snapshot, event window, aggregates, freshness, anomaly evidence." and "Use compact structured schema, discover more capability detail on demand".

O8. Gate. ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-observe-query.test.ts test/workbench-observation.test.ts test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts green; existing tests untouched; src/index.ts, src/workbench/observation.ts and src/workbench/redaction.ts unchanged (git diff --name-only asserts); record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles). Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Independently assignable packages" W16: "compact bounded result and ACL" (the ACL remains the registered tool's host-side check in src/index.ts; this module receives an already-authorized scope).
notes: Sr. Engineer constraint 2026-10-15: pure module; outputs through sanitizeWorkbenchJsonText; cursor and revision semantics preserve projection invariants (scope isolation, out-of-order refusal); byte cap emits an explicit truncation marker, never silent trimming. Base ad3cf6e+.

title: VC-1/W02-A: live adverse-journey tier for the Claude SDK host (mid-stream cancel after native session ID, pre-start abort, invalid model) with requested/acknowledged/terminal receipt; measurement-only, dist imports, never mocked
description:

The code paths exist: src/workflow/runtime.ts RunWorkflowOptions.signal (line 323) finishes the run as { status: "killed", error: "Workflow aborted." } (line 867) after host.abortAgent(agentId) for every in-flight agent (line 853); src/workbench/claude-host.ts keeps one AbortController per agent (lines 98/156), passes it to the SDK query as abortController (line 171), aborts it in abortAgent (line 268) and returns { ok:false, skipped:true, error:"Claude SDK query was cancelled.", sessionId? } (lines 207/218/247), with onMessage/onSettled hooks (lines 42-43). The builder throws if any string field matches /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or contains \x1b (redaction is the runner's job; the receipt must never carry a credential).
2. qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new runner; imports ONLY ../../dist/workbench/claude-host.js, ../../dist/workflow/runtime.js, ../../dist/workbench/redaction.js and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk getSessionInfo; cwd = argv[2] ?? process.cwd(); no vi.mock, no query override, no Pi AgentManager). One real host per journey: createClaudeWorkflowHost({cwd, model: process.env.CLAUDE_ADVERSE_MODEL ?? "claude-opus-5-5", tools: [], settingSources: [], permissionMode: "dontAsk", onMessage, onSettled}).
   J1 mid-stream cancel: the script runs parallel([agent(long prompt A), agent(long prompt B)]) where each prompt asks for about 600 words so the stream outlives the abort; an AbortController passed as the runWorkflow signal is aborted on the FIRST onMessage with type "system", subtype "init" and a session_id (fault location "after Claude SDK session ID first received"); record requestedAt. onSettled records per-agent acknowledgedAt and the host result. runWorkflow resolution records terminalAt and the outcome.

Exit semantics (receipt printed as one JSON line and written to $CLAUDE_ADVERSE_RECEIPT when set, BEFORE exiting): 0 = realised and no findings; 1 = realised with findings (a measured violation, recorded honestly, never tuned away); 2 = not realised (gateway unreachable or unauthenticated, every J1 agent settled before the abort landed, or J3 accepted the model) with a diagnostic naming the unrealised journey. Files: qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new), qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new), test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one additive block).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts fails before qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

J1. Cancellation is explicit, never a completion. After the abort on the first init message, outcome.status === "killed" and outcome.error === "Workflow aborted."; outcome.value is undefined; no agent in flight at requestedAt has a settled result with ok === true; every cancelled agent's settled result is { ok: false, skipped: true, error: "Claude SDK query was cancelled." } carrying the sessionId the SDK reported; agents the SDK finished BEFORE requestedAt are counted as settledBeforeCancel (reported, not a failure), and the journey is realised only if agentsCancelled >= 1, else exit 2. Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Vertical cuts" VC-1: "Ctrl-C/cancel and invalid model/permission failures behave explicitly." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error".

J2. Three phases with their own timestamps. The receipt records requestedAt (abort call), acknowledgedAt per cancelled agent (onSettled delivering the cancellation result) and terminalAt (runWorkflow resolved), with requestedAt <= each acknowledgedAt <= terminalAt; requestToAckMs and ackToTerminalMs are measured numbers; the receipt never reports a phase it did not observe (acknowledgedAt is absent for an agent whose onSettled never fired, and the assessor then records finding "unacknowledged-agent"). Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Cancellation and steering": "Cancellation request != terminal acknowledgement."

J3. Cancellation is scoped to owned sessions and starts nothing new. After requestedAt no further SDK message of type "system"/subtype "init" is observed (initAfterAbort === 0); the number of distinct session_ids equals the number of agents started before requestedAt; every observed session_id matches /^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/ and getSessionInfo(sessionId, {dir: cwd}) returns a record whose sessionId equals it after the run (the native record exists and is neither invented nor deleted). Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-010: "Stopping the parent propagates cancellation only through established ownership and appropriate SDK API; stopping observation does not." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Cancellation and steering": "Keep SDK AbortController (or supported SDK stop API) scoped to exactly one owned Claude invocation." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-009: "Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values."

J4. Pre-start abort creates no native work. With the signal already aborted before runWorkflow, outcome.status === "killed", sdkMessages === 0 and sessionIds is empty. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Before/after Claude SDK session ID first received; during tool execution; after output tokens streamed but before final." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

J5. Invalid model fails explicitly. With the invalid model, outcome.status !== "completed", outcome.error is a non-empty string passed through redactWorkbenchText (at most 400 characters, no control characters), no settled result has ok === true, and sessionIds carries only ids the SDK actually reported (possibly none); if the gateway accepts the model and completes, the journey is unrealised (exit 2, finding "invalid-model-accepted"), never a pass. Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "Negative: invalid model, absent credentials, malformed native output, stream error after partial text, aborted query, resumed unknown session, inaccessible cwd, invalid tool policy." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "Missing fixture settings fail rather than skip. Their receipts establish only the surfaces actually exercised."

J7. Evidence-grade, redacted receipt. The receipt carries contract "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, sdkVersion read from node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json (0.3.300 at HEAD, never hardcoded), model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised and pass; it contains no assistant text, prompt text or tool payload (only ids, types, counts, timestamps and redacted error previews), and the pure builder throws on any value matching /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or containing \x1b. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Streaming and progress": "Avoid printing secrets or tool payloads in overview."

J8. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (no network, no SDK import): an agent in flight at requestedAt that settles ok:true -> finding "completed-after-cancel"; an init message after requestedAt -> finding "init-after-abort"; agentsCancelled === 0 -> realised false; a pre-start journey with sdkMessages 1 -> finding "work-before-start"; an invalid-model journey with status "completed" -> finding "invalid-model-accepted"; a receipt input containing "Authorization: Bearer abc123" -> the builder throws; a clean fixture -> pass true with every J7 field present. title: W22-B: packed npm artifact boundary falsifier (top-level allowlist, agent-tooling denylist, bundled-only node_modules, .npmignore fix for tracked .agents/ and .codex/) plus evidence-grade package-smoke receipt (revision, toolchain, host, pack determinism)
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` packs 374 files including the git-tracked agent-tooling files `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/beads/agents/openai.yaml`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. `.codex/hooks.json` wires `bd codex-hook` commands to SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/PostCompact, so a consumer who opens the installed package directory in Codex inherits hook commands from the npm artifact. `.npmignore` already excludes `.pi`, `.claude`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` under its own heading "Internal contributor/agent instructions — not for distribution" but omits `.agents/` and `.codex/`. qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs (default forge gate step `package-smoke`) denies only the `.beads/` and `.forge/` prefixes, and its receipt `{contract:"workbench.package-smoke/v1", fileCount, sha, integrity, privateStateIncluded}` records no revision, tool versions, timestamp, host or command, contrary to the docs/workbench/14 truth-label rule. Packed `node_modules/` content is today exactly the three `inBundle: true` package-lock entries (@forge/sdk 49 files, @furnace/sdk 79, @hyperunix/sdk 111); nothing asserts that.

Scope (atomic, hot-file free, no src/ edits):

2. `qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs` (new, plain ESM, no dependencies): export TOP_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST (LICENSE, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, package.json, forge.toml, dist, src, docs, examples, qa, vendor, node_modules), DENIED_PREFIXES (.agents/, .codex/, .pi/, .claude/, .beads/, .forge/, .furnace/, .hyperunix/, .reactive-fiber/, .github/, machines/, test/, tests/), DENIED_BASENAMES (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, biome.json, tsconfig.json), DENIED_PATTERNS (basename matches /\.jsonl$/, /^vitest\..*config\.ts$/ or /\.test\.ts$/), `classifyPackedPaths(paths, { bundledLockEntries })` returning `{ violations: {path, rule}[], topLevel: string[] }` where a `node_modules/` path is a violation unless its (scope-aware) package name is in bundledLockEntries (the package-lock `packages` entry names whose `inBundle === true`), and a pure `buildPackageReceipt(input)` that assembles the v2 receipt from already-measured values.
3. `qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs`: keep every existing v1 assertion verbatim; add classifyPackedPaths over the pack listing (any violation fails the smoke listing every offending path and rule); pack the same tree a second time and assert identical `shasum` and `integrity`; emit receipt `contract: "workbench.package-smoke/v2"` with the v1 fields plus revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, or the literal `unknown:not-a-git-checkout`), dirty (true/false from `git status --porcelain`, or null when revision is unknown), node (process.version), npm (`npm --version`), platform, arch, utc, command, topLevel (sorted), bundled (sorted lock entry names), denied (always [] on success).
4. `test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts` (new vitest; no npm child process, no network): imports the classifier and receipt builder from `../qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs`, runs the fixture cases in acceptance item 6, unit-tests the receipt builder with fake git results, and parses `.npmignore` asserting the required exclusion lines.

Out of scope (flag in the ledger line, do not change): whether `qa/` development runners and `docs/` should ship; a package.json `exports` map; version bump; npm publication; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md or docs/workbench/*; forge.toml. If any step needs a hot file or a src/ change, stop and return blocked.

Files: .npmignore; qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs; qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs (new); test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts (new).

title: W13/VC-2: Forge gate-status reader adapter projects NativeSnapshots and grouping edges (historical last_result stays unknown/partial, failed gate stays failed); tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap: the only NativeSnapshot producer in src/ is FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, extended by wb-752.1); grep -rn "NativeSnapshot\|projectionSnapshot" src returns only that file and its hot consumer src/index.ts:2560. The real native Forge read (src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, invoke() result {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source}) never reaches the ObservationProjection or the inspector. docs/workbench/09 § Reader adapters requires a read-current-snapshot function per supported provider, and docs/workbench/15 gates the P1 inspector release on "real native source". The measured native read of this workspace returned status=success with authoritative_current=false, which must appear as historical/indeterminate, never as a verified PASS.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exporting
- forgeGateTopology(reading: JsonValue, context: { scope: ObservationScope; target: string; capturedAt: string; observedAt: string; invocationId?: string }): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ForgeObservedRelation[]; diagnostics: string[] } where ForgeObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate.
- Validation: reading must be the exact provider output (contract 'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.status', source.envelope.reason_code string, source.data.packages an array of objects with a string ref of at most 256 bytes and no control characters); anything else throws CapabilityError('validation'). Unknown extra producer fields are tolerated, never required and never copied into presentation text.
- One workspace snapshot: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id:'workspace', scope: context.target}, kind 'forge.gate.status.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText built from source.status, envelope.verdict and envelope.reason_code (e.g. "partial · COULD_NOT_JUDGE · FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE · verification indeterminate"), statusTone 'unknown' unless every package is authoritative_current === true (then 'failure' if any last_result === 'failure', 'success' only if all last_result === 'success'), coverage 'partial' when source.status !== 'success' or any package is not authoritative_current, otherwise 'complete'; sourceVersion 'forge.gate.status/v1'; evidenceRefs ['forge:gate.status:<reason_code>'].
- One snapshot per package: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id: pkg.ref, scope: context.target}, statusText "<last_result> (historical; authoritative_current=false[; <unverified_reason>])" with statusTone 'unknown' whenever authoritative_current !== true; when authoritative_current === true, statusText "<last_result> (current)" with statusTone 'success' for last_result 'success', 'failure' for 'failure', 'unknown' otherwise. Never an interval (Forge gate status carries no timestamps), never subjectBasis (a target path is not a basis), never definitionDigest.
- One 'grouping' relation workspace->package per package with provenance {source:'forge-observer', observedAt: context.observedAt}; never 'ownership' (the gate.status envelope carries no native lifecycle confirmation reference, and relate() rejects ownership without one) and never 'dependency'/'causation'/'hypothesis'.
- All presentation text passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts, hot — do not edit) and is bounded to 200 characters so ObservationProjection.refresh never throws on producer text.

Out of scope: registering or wiring the adapter into furnace_observe/workflow_observe (src/index.ts, hot), providers/forge.ts changes (the adapter consumes its output), inspector text assertions or changes (wb-6ze.1 owns src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts this round), any Forge write or gate.run.
Files: src/workbench/forge-observer.ts (new); test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts (new). Fixture: reuse the SOURCE shape from test/workbench-forge-contract.test.ts.
acceptance_criteria:

With SOURCE = {status:'success', envelope:{verdict:null, reason_code:'FORGE_OK'}, data:{packages:[{ref:'code:pi-subagents', last_result:'success', authoritative_current:false, unverified_reason:'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED'}]}} wrapped as {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source: SOURCE}: exactly two snapshots; the package snapshot has statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'historical', 'authoritative_current=false' and 'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED', coverage 'partial'; JSON.stringify(result) does not contain '"statusTone":"success"'. Quote docs/workbench/00-current-state-and-source-map.md § "2026-10-15 implementation update (experimental; evidence-scoped)": "authoritative_current=false (historical status, not current verification). That latter field is preserved without a fabricated PASS." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-015: "Workbench cannot turn absent/unknown/partial producer evidence into successful domain verdict."

F2 Failed gate stays failed; current success is success. authoritative_current true with last_result 'failure' -> package statusTone 'failure' and workspace statusTone 'failure' even though source.status is 'success'; authoritative_current true with last_result 'success' -> 'success' and coverage 'complete'. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 7: "A true Forge failed gate remains failed despite transport success." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem" Forge row: "gate on exact candidate/basis with producer verdict | source basis changed -> no PASS".

F3 Partial envelope is indeterminate, not empty success. {status:'partial', envelope:{verdict:'COULD_NOT_JUDGE', reason_code:'FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE'}, data:{packages:[]}} -> one workspace snapshot with statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'COULD_NOT_JUDGE' and 'indeterminate', coverage 'partial', zero package snapshots, zero relations, and one diagnostic naming the empty package list. Quote docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Registration and resolution": "validate output representation without erasing unknown producer fields."

Every relation has kind 'grouping' and provenance.source 'forge-observer'; relations.length === packages.length; no snapshot carries interval, subjectBasis or definitionDigest. F6 Read-model integration. Applying snapshots via ObservationProjection.refresh and relations via relate on a real projection: query({scope, parent: workspaceRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the package nodes; query({scope, statusTone:'unknown', limit: 10}) includes the historical package; every relations({scope, from: workspaceKey}) entry is 'grouping'; a second forgeGateTopology call with the same reading and a later observedAt refreshes without duplicating nodes (stats().nodes unchanged). Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Reader adapters": "Reader adapter returns snapshot {nativeRef, capturedAt, observedAt, sourceRevision?, coverage?, nativePayloadRef}". Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Gating policy": "P1 inspector release requires VC-4/VC-5 with real native source and scale benchmark."

F7 Bounded, redacted presentation. A reason_code of 10,000 characters containing 'Bearer abc123' and '\x1b[31m' yields statusText of at most 200 characters with no control characters, containing '[REDACTED]' and not 'abc123', and refresh() does not throw. Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display (no untrusted ANSI injection)." Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default."

F8 Native status is not replaced by tone. statusText always contains the literal native last_result / verdict strings; the test asserts that native 'success' and tone 'unknown' coexist in the F1 package snapshot. title: W14/VC-5: Incremental ancestor aggregates over observed grouping/ownership edges in ObservationProjection (measured counts, interval envelope, incomplete-trace label; inspector wiring excluded)
description:
Gap: ObservationProjection (src/workbench/observation.ts) keeps flat per-node indexes (status, kind, basis, evidence, version, time) but no ancestor aggregate: nothing answers "how many observed children/descendants does this group or Run have, in which status tones, with which interval envelope" without re-walking relations per frame. docs/workbench/10 requires ancestor aggregates to be maintained incrementally and the overview to show "status and counts"; docs/workbench/09 § Aggregates and profiling requires measured counts with an explicit "incomplete trace" label instead of a precise critical path. wb-9x5.2 (W21-A, seat g1) explicitly deferred "adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts" to a follow-up; wb-6ze.1 (W15 nested tree) is confined to the inspector and uses no new projection API. This bead supplies the read-model half only.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free), all inside src/workbench/observation.ts:
- export interface AncestorAggregate { key: string; revision: number; topologyRevision: number; direct: { children: number; settled: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number> }; descendants: { counted: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number>; stale: number; depthReached: number; truncated: boolean }; intervals: { known: number; missing: number; open: number; earliestStartedAt?: string; latestEndedAt?: string }; trace: "incomplete" | "bounded"; criticalPath: "unestablished"; basis: "observed-grouping-ownership" }
- aggregate(filter: { scope: ObservationScope; key: string }): AncestorAggregate | undefined — a copied value; undefined for unknown or cross-scope keys without any traversal.
- aggregateStats(): { adjustments: number; rebuilds: number; maxVisitedPerUpdate: number } (additive; the existing stats() shape {nodes, events, edges} is unchanged).
Child edges are outgoing relations of kind 'grouping' or 'ownership' (parent = from, child = to). Set semantics: a descendant is counted once per ancestor even through diamonds. Depth cap AGGREGATE_DEPTH = 8 (same cap as wb-6ze.1); cycles terminate at the first repeated key. 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never trigger or contribute. Hot path: a node's status/interval/freshness change (ingest, refresh, markStale, disconnect, reconnect) adjusts its ancestors by walking incoming grouping/ownership edges with a per-walk visited set — O(depth x fan-in), never a scan of nodes or events. Topology changes (relate/removeEdge of grouping/ownership edges, discard/eviction) rebuild only the affected ancestors from their bounded subtree. settled = success + failure tones; stale = descendants whose freshness !== 'current'; intervals use source intervals only (earliest startedAt, latest endedAt; an open interval increments open and never fabricates an end); trace is 'incomplete' whenever intervals.missing > 0 or descendants.truncated; criticalPath is the literal 'unestablished' (no number, no estimate, no token or cost fields).

Out of scope: rendering counts in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (reserved this round by wb-6ze.1 and wb-g1g.1; a later bead wires overview counts), workflow_observe tool output (src/index.ts, hot), supernode collapse, concurrency/critical-path profiling, any cap change.
Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (edit, additive); test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation*.test.ts, test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts and test/workbench-inspector*.test.ts stay verbatim and green.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts fails before aggregate()/aggregateStats() exist. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1 Brute-force equality (falsifier). A seeded deterministic fixture (no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts) builds >= 500 nodes with grouping and ownership edges up to depth 8 including diamonds, plus dependency/causation/hypothesis edges; after every batch of status/interval/freshness mutations and edge additions, aggregate(key) for every key deep-equals an independent brute-force recomputation over grouping/ownership reachability with set semantics. Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened."

A2 Only observed hierarchy counts. A dependency/causation/hypothesis-only fixture yields direct.children === 0 and descendants.counted === 0 for every key; adding a 'grouping' edge changes the parent's aggregate, adding a 'hypothesis' edge between the same pair does not. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)", "grouping only (phase, display scope)", "inferred possible relationship (hypothesis; never treated as authoritative)". Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-037: "Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable."

A3 Incremental propagation and depth cap. On a 10-level grouping chain, flipping the leaf from active to success increments descendants.byTone.success and settled at each ancestor within 8 levels, leaves the 9th and 10th ancestors unchanged with descendants.truncated === true and depthReached === 8, and aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 for that flip. Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-029: "Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame."

A4 Cycles and diamonds terminate. Grouping cycle A->B->A: both aggregates are finite (descendants.counted === 1 each), the test completes, depthReached <= 8; a diamond P->X, P->Y, X->Z, Y->Z counts Z once in aggregate(P) (descendants.counted === 3). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan."

A5 Eviction and edge removal subtract. With maxNodes/maxEdges limits forcing FIFO eviction, discarding a counted child or evicting its grouping edge brings the ancestors' counts back to the brute-force value; stats() keeps the existing {nodes, events, edges} shape so test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts toEqual stays green. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Derived view indexes": "Coalesce same-node repeated updates; do not rebuild entire history on each render."

A6 Measured intervals, no fabricated timing. Descendants with intervals give earliestStartedAt/latestEndedAt equal to the min startedAt / max endedAt of source intervals; a descendant with an open interval increments intervals.open and leaves latestEndedAt undefined; a descendant without an interval increments intervals.missing and sets trace 'incomplete'; criticalPath === 'unestablished' always, and JSON.stringify(aggregate) contains no numeric critical-path, token, cost or estimated field. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics. If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show \"incomplete trace\". Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Overview: "Critical path must be shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete."

A7 Freshness rollup. disconnect('furnace') raises descendants.stale to the number of non-current descendants; reconnect alone leaves it unchanged; a refresh() snapshot lowers it. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale." and "UI shows STALE/UNKNOWN visibly."

A8 Bounded work at scale. A 2,000-node, 5-level grouped tree receiving 100,000 status ingests: aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 and aggregateStats().rebuilds does not grow with status updates (rebuilds count only topology changes); the median per-ingest time at 200 nodes vs 2,000 nodes is printed in the test output (reported, not asserted beyond the visit bound). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-045: "Hierarchical agent-swarm aggregation and profile comparisons handle 10k+ nodes subject to benchmarked limits."

A9 Scope isolation. aggregate() with a key from another workspace/principal returns undefined and leaves aggregateStats() unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls."

title: W16-A: pure workflow_control decision module (grant+confirmed-ownership preconditions, observer-only and guessed-action refusal, requested/acknowledged/result receipt); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Every `workflow_*` Pi tool and every `workbench:*` grant check lives in src/index.ts (hot, Sr. Engineer-owned), and native Furnace control would live in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts (hot). W16's acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" still needs a testable control core. Deliver it as ONE new source file and ONE new test file; register nothing.

src/workbench/control.ts (new), pure and provider-free:
- `interface NativeControlRequest { scope: ObservationScope; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; grants: readonly string[] | undefined; target: NativeRef; action: string; params?: JsonValue; invocationId: string; requestedAt: string }` (names follow docs/workbench/13 Host boundary `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`; this bead implements the decision, not the host method).
- `decideControl(request, deps: { projection: ObservationProjection; now: () => string })` returns `{ decision: 'denied'; category: CapabilityErrorCategory; reason: string }` or `{ decision: 'permitted'; receipt: NativeControlReceipt }`.
- `NativeControlReceipt` phases are distinct and ordered: `requested` -> `acknowledged` -> `result`. Fields: contractVersion 'workbench.control/v1', requestId, principal, grant, policy (rule name), target, action, invocationId, ownershipConfirmationRef, requestedAt; `acknowledge(receipt, { acknowledgedAt, nativeAckRef })` and `settle(receipt, { outcome: 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'unknown'; nativeResultRef: string; settledAt })` return new frozen receipts and throw CapabilityError('validation') on out-of-order transitions or missing native references. The module never calls a provider, never mutates the projection, never fabricates acknowledged/result.
- Deny rules (first match wins, every rule has a test): grants undefined/non-array/non-string entries or any wildcard (`control:*`) -> authorization "unknown permission data"; grants containing only discover:/inspect:/observe: prefixes -> authorization "observer-only" regardless of action spelling (stop, STOP, terminate, __proto__); action not in the frozen per-provider allowlist (furnace: stop; claude-agent-sdk: interrupt; forge: cancel) -> validation "unknown action"; missing exact grant `control:<provider>.<action>` -> authorization; target key not in the request scope (different workspace/principal) -> authorization "cross-scope"; target lacking a projection `ownership` relation whose provenance.source === target.provider AND provenance.nativeConfirmationRef is a non-empty string (re-check both; do not trust the relation kind alone) -> authorization "no confirmed lifecycle ownership" (causation/grouping/hypothesis edges never qualify); destructive actions (stop, cancel, interrupt, kill, delete) without `params.confirmed === true` -> validation "operator confirmation required".
test/workbench-control.test.ts (new): one test per rule plus the phase-ordering falsifiers; no TTY, no providers, no network.
Out of scope: any edit to src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts or other hot files; Pi tool registration; executing a native stop. If the worker finds registration necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.

• export interface ClaudeEvidenceContent { contract: typeof CLAUDE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'claude.transcript.message'; provider: 'claude-agent-sdk'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'message', id: uuid, scope: sessionId}); role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system' (the row type); capturedAt; bytes: number (UTF-8 byte length of the selected row's text as returned by the reader); truncated: boolean (bytes > maxBytes or more than maxLines lines); preview: readonly string[] (the selected row's text split on newlines, each line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters, at most maxLines lines, plus a final '… truncated (budget)' line whenever truncated); producerReceipt: { sessionId: string; windowLimit: number; returned: number (rows the reader returned); rowIndex: number (position of the selected row in that window) }; freshness: 'current' } — the docs/20 EvidenceContent shape minus store-level fields, so the claude EvidenceLoader of the wb-g1g.1 follow-up returns it after applying the owning node's freshness.
• export async function readClaudeMessageEvidence(request: ClaudeEvidenceRequest): Promise<ClaudeEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any read (each a CapabilityError, reader never called): grants() not an array, containing non-string entries or any wildcard entry (claude:*, *) -> 'authorization' ("unknown permission data"); missing the exact literal 'claude:transcript' (case-sensitive; 'claude:Transcript', 'transcript', 'claude:*' do not count) -> 'authorization' ("claude:transcript grant required"); owningSessionNode.nativeRef.provider !== 'claude-agent-sdk' || type !== 'session' || id !== sessionId -> 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a Claude session node of this scope"; a pre-init {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call'} node, index.ts:2683, is refused because it carries no native session identity); evidenceRef absent from owningSessionNode.evidenceRefs -> 'authorization' (a message of another session is unauthorized); evidenceRef not matching /^claude-message:([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119})$/ -> 'validation'; windowLimit, maxBytes, maxLines or timeoutMs out of range, or sessionId/cwd empty -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Claude evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one readTranscript(sessionId, cwd, windowLimit) call, raced against request.signal and timeoutMs (abort -> 'transport'; timeout -> 'transport' naming the budget; the reader promise is abandoned, never awaited further). Row validation: every returned row must be an object with type in user|assistant|system, string uuid and string text, else 'unavailable' ("malformed transcript row shape"). Selection: the first row whose uuid === the requested uuid; none inside the returned window -> CapabilityError('transport', "message <uuid> is outside the bounded transcript window (<returned> of limit <windowLimit>)") — never a synthesized row, never a neighbouring row. A thrown reader error is rethrown as CapabilityError('unavailable', preview) where preview is the message through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters, never verbatim. The content never retains the window: no field named rows, lines, message, messages, raw, data or payload, and no other row's text appears anywhere in JSON.stringify(content).

title: W14/VC-5-C: pure attention and bottleneck selector over ObservationProjection (waiting/stale/unknown/disconnected counts, top measured open intervals from source intervals, dependency-chain critical path only as partial-estimated else incomplete-trace with reasons; caller clock, bounded, sanitized); inspector and tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Overview) requires "status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" with the critical path "shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete", and docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling" requires measured-vs-estimated separation with "incomplete trace" whenever intervals or dependencies are missing. Today src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:156-157 prints two CONSTANT strings regardless of data ('Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress.' and 'Critical path: incomplete trace (no complete dependency/interval proof).'), pinned by test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:112-116 and :195-198. Nothing in src/ computes attention items, bottlenecks or a dependency-chain estimate from observed data: grep -rn 'bottleneck\|criticalPath' src returns only designer.ts:183/236 (criticalPath "unestablished" for run comparisons; hot, untouched) and the inspector constants. wb-6ze.2 (ancestor aggregates in observation.ts) pins criticalPath 'unestablished' and lists "concurrency/critical-path profiling" out of scope; wb-6ze.1 owns the inspector file this run; wb-752.2 builds the workflow_observe reply. This bead supplies the pure selector both consumers wire later.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/attention.ts exporting
• ATTENTION_CONTRACT = "workbench.attention/v1".
• selectAttention(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; now: string; limit?: number; bottlenecks?: number }): AttentionReport.
• AttentionReport = { contract: typeof ATTENTION_CONTRACT; basis: "observed"; now: string; examined: { nodes: number; truncated: boolean }; counts: { active; waiting; success; failure; unknown; stale; disconnected; withInterval; withoutInterval }; disconnectedProviders: string[]; bottlenecks: { key; nativeRef; title; tone; freshness; openMs: number; measured: true }[]; unmeasured: number; clockSkew: number; criticalPath: { label: "incomplete-trace"; reasons: ("no-dependency-edges" | "missing-intervals" | "open-intervals" | "hypothesis-edges" | "cycle" | "truncated")[] } | { label: "partial-estimated"; keys: string[]; measuredMs: number; coverage: { chainNodes: number; dependencyEdges: number }; caveat: string }; clockCaveat: string }.
• Rules. `now` is the CALLER's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now()). Nodes come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit: input.limit ?? 100}) call; examined.truncated propagates its truncated flag. openMs = now − interval.startedAt for nodes with statusTone 'active' or 'waiting' that have interval.startedAt and no endedAt; a producer startedAt later than now clamps openMs to 0 and increments clockSkew; nodes without an interval are counted in unmeasured and never ranked; ranking is openMs descending then key ascending (deterministic); bottlenecks.length <= input.bottlenecks ?? 5 and every entry carries measured: true. counts.stale = nodes with freshness !== 'current'; counts.disconnected = nodes with sourceConnectionState 'disconnected'; disconnectedProviders = sorted distinct nativeRef.provider of those nodes. Tones are counted separately (waiting is never folded into active or stale).
• criticalPath. Dependency edges come from projection.relations({scope, from: key, limit}) for examined keys only, kind 'dependency' only. 'partial-estimated' requires ALL of: at least one dependency edge among examined nodes; no 'hypothesis' edge among examined nodes; no cycle on dependency edges; query not truncated; every node on the chosen chain has a COMPLETE interval (startedAt and endedAt). measuredMs is the sum of complete interval durations along the longest-duration dependency chain (DAG longest path); keys lists that chain in dependency order; the caveat literal is "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence." Anything else returns incomplete-trace carrying EVERY applicable reason. The label is never "exact" or "complete" and no number is emitted without the partial-estimated label.
• clockCaveat literal: "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."
• Every title passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts; do not edit) and is cut to 120 characters; control characters never survive; JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384 at limit 100 / bottlenecks 5.

Out of scope: rendering in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 / wb-g1g.1 territory this run), the workflow_observe reply (wb-752.2) and src/index.ts, any edit to src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 owns the aggregate API; this bead only CALLS query/relations), token/cost/retry metrics (no producer supplies them), designer.ts (hot).
